publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/__tests__/cron-cadence.test.ts (26), mutation-verified. The cron path changed here is a CADENCE gate, and the new non-operator decision point is claimOncePerShopDay() in server/cron/scheduler.ts — it decides whether a business-hours job may run today. It FAILS CLOSED at every exit: outside business hours -> false; getDb() null -> false; any thrown error -> a log.warn carrying errorId CRON_DAILY_CLAIM_FAILED, then false. That direction is deliberate and asymmetric: two of the four jobs on this path (referral-loop-closer, vip-auto-recognition) send customer SMS, so a DB blip returning `true` would re-fire them on every pass of the 2h tier. A duplicate text costs more than a missed day. The claim also sits INSIDE acquireCronLock(job.name) and releases the lock when it declines — two pods that each read 'not yet run today' would otherwise both claim and both send, which is the v1.7 duplicate-SMS regression this repo already paid for. Tests pin all three properties directly: fail-closed on unreadable claim (asserts the `if (!d) return false` exit and a catch that returns false), the claim-after-lock ordering, and the lock release on a declined claim. Three mutations were verified to turn the suite RED and the file restored byte-identical after each: a businessHoursOnly job moved back into the 24h daily tier (1 fail), the claim moved before the lock (2 fails), and the ET clock replaced by a hardcoded -05:00 offset (5 fails). Full serial suite green: 376 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,622 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone — the tire cockpit (/admin, Tire Commerce Command Center). Reproducible with no production access: point DATABASE_URL at a dead host and open the section. BEFORE: six metric tiles read "New Requests 0 / Confirmed 0 / Ordered-In Transit 0 / Ready to Install 0 / Installed 0 / Tire Revenue $0", and the list below rendered "No tire orders found — Try adjusting your active filters or query". Every number a confident zero, and the copy blaming the operator's own filters for a database outage. AFTER: one amber strip above the grid — "Tire order counts could not be read. The tiles below are unknown — NOT zero." — all six tiles show an em dash, and the list renders the red "Failed to load orders / Please sync or try again later" panel. ★ THE POINT OF THIS ONE: that red panel ALREADY EXISTED and had never fired. TireOrdersSection.tsx:310 branches on `isError` and has since it was written; the router returned `{ orders: [], total: 0 }` on an unreadable database, tRPC resolved HTTP 200, react-query kept isError false, and the correct error UI sat dead below an empty state that claimed the shop had no orders. Not one client line was needed to bring it back — only the server throw. orderStats was the opposite shape: no error channel existed at all, six tiles read `stats?.x ?? 0`, so that half is the em-dash + amber-strip idiom from money/UnpaidInvoicesSection.tsx:29, static rather than a toast because this query refetches every 60s on the counter screen. A genuine counted 0 is unchanged and still reads as an honest empty pipeline. NOT CHANGED, deliberately: every publicProcedure on the same router still degrades quietly — publicStats, checkOrder, placeOrder, createCheckout and getTireMarkup render on customer pages and sit on the order path, where a thrown error costs a sale while a missing social-proof line costs nothing. Two tests assert that asymmetry directly rather than leaving it to a comment. cancellationRisks and getOrder were left alone for a different reason: neither has a client consumer, so neither renders a false all-clear today. EVIDENCE: server/ros083TireCockpit.test.ts (7), MUTATION-VERIFIED — restoring the orderStats early return turns 3 cases red, and the router file was restored byte-identical (0 residual markers, diff back to 21 insertions / 2 deletions). Full serial suite green (figures in the PR body). tsc --noEmit clean. NOT CLAIMED: no live production observation — verified by forcing db() to null, not by taking prod down. NOTE ON THIS KEY: last-writer-wins by design — the manifest lives on main while requirements are derived per-diff, so this text describes the most recently merged operator-facing change and nothing else; git log on this file is the history.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on one new file under server/services/**: reelReliability.ts. That file is a VERBATIM extraction of the getReelReliability body out of routers/instagramAdmin.ts — verified by diffing the logic lines, which are byte-identical; the only deltas are the `unknown` literal gaining an explicit ReelReliability annotation (same eight fields, same null values) and the sibling import path changing from ../services/reelRecoverability to ./reelRecoverability. The router now delegates in two lines. Nothing nickstire CAN DO changed: no new surface is exposed, no capability changes operationalState, no provider, cost, publish or generation path is touched, and the healthy path is behaviourally identical. The extraction exists so the admin console and the operator's phone read the SAME arithmetic instead of two copies that drift. The other two nickstire edits: (a) two READ-ONLY delegates added to the nour-os-query QUERY_HANDLERS map (instagram_delivery_issues, instagram_reel_reliability), each a one-line call into an existing service; (b) an ADDITIVE dbReadable:!!db field on the pre-existing instagram_autopost_status handler, so an unreadable log table can be told apart from an idle lane — additive because the other consumer of that query (statenour lib/ai/tools/social.ts) hands the raw result to an LLM and reads no specific field, so nothing can break. The operator-facing change is entirely on the statenour side (/ig Telegram commands), which this ledger does not track; the nearest entry, operator-command-center, describes the admin console and is unaffected. EVIDENCE: apps/statenour/tests/telegram/ig-format.test.ts (17) pins the rendering contract that null means UNKNOWN and never zero — an all-null ReelReliability renders 'UNKNOWN, not healthy' rather than '0 jobs', and dbReadable:false renders unknown rather than 'No autopost runs recorded'. Both verified by FALSIFICATION, not assumed: disabling each guard turns exactly the corresponding test red and leaves the compatibility test passing. nickstire: 22 test files / 333 passed / exit 0, including adminPermissionCoverage and bridge-shapes. statenour: 428 files / 4824 passed / 1 skipped / exit 0. NOT CLAIMED: the webhook wiring (igBridgeError / igRead / dispatch) has no direct test — that route has never had one and testing it needs prisma + journal-brain mocks. The rendering logic, where the risk lives, is fully covered. PR #1331.
